Download the Hansard database

Source: R/data-download.R
db_download.Rd

Downloads the full Hansard database that this version of ausparl was released with, from its Zenodo version record. The file is about 9.5 GB. An interrupted download resumes where it stopped when you call db_download() again with the same arguments. The file is installed only once its MD5 checksum matches the one Zenodo lists.

Usage

db_download(force = FALSE, dir = NULL, background = FALSE)

Arguments

force

If TRUE, download again even when a verified copy is already installed.

dir

A directory to install the database in, as a single string. NULL (the default) uses the ausparl user data directory.

background

If TRUE, run the download in the background (an RStudio background job, or a separate R process) and return straight away. See the section "In the background".

Value

The path of the installed database file, invisibly. With background = TRUE, the path it will be installed at, returned before the download finishes.

Details

Where it goes. By default the database is installed in the ausparl user data directory (tools::R_user_dir("ausparl", "data"); set the R_USER_DATA_DIR environment variable to move it), and db_connect() with no arguments then opens it, unless you pass path, sample = TRUE or set the AUSPARL_DB environment variable, which take precedence.

With dir, the database is installed directly in that directory as hansard.duckdb (the directory is created if needed), for example db_download(dir = "dataset") in a project folder. db_connect() with no arguments finds that copy only when it is in the working directory or its dataset/ folder, or after it was opened once in the session; elsewhere, open it with db_connect(path = file.path(dir, "hansard.duckdb")) or set AUSPARL_DB. A verified copy of the same database version already in dir is reused; a copy of another version is replaced.

In the background. With background = TRUE the download runs outside your R session, so you can keep working while it runs. In RStudio it runs as a background job, which shows its progress in the Background Jobs pane. Elsewhere (Positron, R in a terminal) it runs in a separate R process that writes its progress to a log file, whose path is printed; that process keeps going if you close your R session. Either way the download is the same: it resumes, is checksum-verified, and is installed in the same place. When it has finished, connect with db_connect() as usual.

One download at a time. While a download runs, a lock file (hansard.duckdb.lock) sits next to the partial download. Calling db_download() again for the same place meanwhile is an error that reports how much has been downloaded so far. A lock left by a download that was killed is removed automatically when it was made on the same computer; on Windows, or for a lock made on another computer (for example in a synced folder), the error says which file to delete.

db_connect() never downloads anything itself. Each ausparl release pins exactly one database version, so an older ausparl never fetches a newer database it cannot read. To use a different database version, install the ausparl release that pins it.

See also

db_connect(), db_info()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# About 9.5 GB; run once per database version.
db_download()
db_connect()
db_info()
db_disconnect()

# Or into a folder of your project, then open it by path.
path <- db_download(dir = "dataset")
db_connect(path = path)

# In the background, so you can keep working; connect once it has finished.
db_download(background = TRUE)
} # }
